item.title: KNOWCASE Open Call 2027: permanent digital-culture installation in Madrid (Sonar+D x Fundacion Cotec)
item.description:
Organisation: Fundacion Cotec and Sonar+D

Location: Installation at the KNOWCASE storefront of Fundacion Cotec's headquarters in Chamberi, Madrid, Spain, a street-level venue visible 24/7. The call is international; applications accepted in Spanish, other official languages of Spain, or English.

Award: Up to EUR 100,000 (plus VAT), all-inclusive: conceptualisation, design, technical development, production, installation, maintenance, documentation, artist fees, travel, accommodation and insurance.

Duration: Installation displayed for a minimum of 24 months, starting February 2027

Deadline: 07 Sep 2026

Fundacion Cotec (a Spanish innovation-focused non-profit) and Sonar+D, building on an initial experiment at Sonar 2026, invite proposals for a long-term installation at KNOWCASE, the street-level showcase of Cotec's Madrid headquarters in Chamberi, visible to the public 24 hours a day. THEME: digital culture, meaning projects that combine knowledge, research, science and data with art, technology and social impact. Cotec's stated priorities are the big transitions (analogue to digital, linear to circular economy, tangible to intangible) plus innovation ecosystems and R&D&I, the climate crisis, the future of work and learning, social divides, citizen participation and democratic health. WHAT YOU GET: a budget of up to EUR 100,000 plus VAT covering everything (design, production, installation, maintenance, documentation, artist fees, travel, accommodation and insurance), and a minimum 24-month public display from February 2027. WHO CAN APPLY: artists, collectives, designers, technologists, universities, research centres, startups, businesses, creative agencies, producers, cultural institutions and multidisciplinary teams, internationally; applicants must demonstrate solid experience and a relevant portfolio. CONSTRAINTS: the proposal must be original and never previously exhibited, must include participative or interactive elements, must encourage critical thinking, and must be technically and financially viable for the full 24+ month exhibition period (durability and maintenance are central selection criteria). Selection weighs conceptual quality highest (40 percent), followed by public interactivity (25 percent). HOW TO APPLY: one PDF of maximum 15 pages containing summary, concept, technical proposal, visuals, budget, timeline, team profile, portfolio and declaration, in Spanish, another official language of Spain, or English, via the application portal linked from the terms and conditions. Results announced 14 October 2026. Deadline 7 September 2026 at midnight CEST.

item.title: Project Liberty: Co-Lab Fund Micro-Grants (Round 2, 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Project Liberty (Alliance SteerCo); pooled fund supported by Future of Life Institute, Omidyar Network, Ergo Impact, and Project Liberty

Location: Members of the Project Liberty coalition (Alliance). Projects led by a Coalition member organization; geography otherwise unrestricted.

Award: Micro-grants of USD 10,000 or less, a deliberate change from Round 1's larger awards so the Fund reaches more of the Coalition. Preference given to organizations that did not receive a Round 1 award. No application fee.

Duration: Short, discrete projects. Applicants must be ready to begin substantive work within two weeks of approval. This is the final round of the summer; the Fund is expected to resume later in 2026.

Deadline: Closed 29 Jul 2026

MEMBERS ONLY: this is a member-led collaboration fund, not an open public call. Projects must be led by a Project Liberty Coalition (Alliance) member organization. Round 2 shifts to micro-grants of USD 10,000 or less, an iterative change from Round 1 intended to spread support across more of the Coalition; organizations that did not receive a Round 1 award are preferred. SCOPE: micro-grants fund two kinds of work, (1) discrete projects that strengthen the Coalition itself, such as Shared Services or convenings, and (2) time-sensitive collaborative projects within a designated workstream. In both cases the work should begin quickly and produce something concrete. A STRONG APPLICATION SHOWS: work that builds the Coalition as an entity, such as shared tools, infrastructure or connections that make joint action easier; clear alignment with a Coalition workstream; value for multiple Coalition organizations; a strong case that the work would not happen, or would move more slowly, without the Fund; a concrete outcome such as a tool, resource, convening, campaign or research product; and readiness to begin substantive work within two weeks of approval. LIMIT: one application per organization, submitted through the existing Co-Lab Fund application form. Round 1 results were still pending at the time of this call, with funded projects to be shared soon and engagement opportunities expected across the work. Prospective applicants unsure whether an idea fits this round are invited to reach out first. DEADLINE: 29 July 2026 at midnight. Background on the Co-Lab program is in the Coalition's overview document.

Open call details

item.title: Project Liberty: Co-Lab Fund Member Collaboration Grants (Round 1, 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Project Liberty (Alliance SteerCo); pooled fund supported by Future of Life Institute, Omidyar Network, Ergo Impact, and Project Liberty

Location: Members of the Project Liberty coalition (Alliance). Projects led by a Coalition member organization; geography otherwise unrestricted.

Award: Grants cap at USD 250,000 per project; most first-round awards fall between USD 25,000 and USD 100,000. Pooled fund supported by Future of Life Institute, Omidyar Network, Ergo Impact, and Project Liberty. No application fee.

Duration: Project length varies. Funding rounds run monthly until December 2026, or until the funds are disbursed; decisions are expected within roughly three weeks of each deadline.

Deadline: Closed 21 Jun 2026

MEMBERS ONLY: this is a member-led collaboration fund, not an open public call. Projects must be led by a Project Liberty Coalition (Alliance) member organization. The Co-Lab Fund, launched by the coalition's Steering Committee (SteerCo), supports projects that Coalition members undertake together, building on the trust and relationships that already exist within the community so that funding decisions can rest on the strength of the idea, the people behind it, and their track records rather than extensive diligence. In exchange for a streamlined process, grants stay modest and funded teams share their progress with the broader Coalition as projects develop, creating accountability and letting the community learn from what emerges. Two kinds of projects qualify: (1) work that advances the Coalition's active workstreams (listed in the application), and (2) investment in the Coalition's connective infrastructure, such as shared services and resources that strengthen collective capacity. Eligibility: projects must be led by a Coalition member organization, produce value for more than one Coalition organization, begin substantive work within a few weeks of approval, and fall within the active workstreams; full eligibility details are in the Overview and FAQ document. How it works: monthly rounds are planned until December 2026 or until the funds are disbursed; the application is designed to take an hour or less once the project's shape is clear, and decisions are expected within about three weeks of each deadline. This is the first cycle and the Fund is being built as it goes, so the process is expected to improve each round. Round 1 closes Sunday, 21 June 2026; further rounds follow, so there is no need to force an idea into this cycle. Apply via the Fillout application form.

Open call details

item.title: GitHub Secure Open Source Fund
item.description:
Organisation: GitHub

Location: Remote (GitHub Sponsors-supported regions)

Award: $10,000 per project via GitHub Sponsors ($6,000 at the kickoff sprint, $2,000 at 6 months, $2,000 at 12 months), plus security training and community. No application fee.

Duration: 12-month engagement

Deadline: Rolling / undated

GitHub's Secure Open Source Fund supports maintainers to improve the security of widely-used open-source software, pairing funding with hands-on security training. ELIGIBILITY: individual maintainers or teams of up to three, aged 18 or older, in a region supported by GitHub Sponsors; applicants cannot work for GitHub or its parent company. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis; apply once to be considered for upcoming 2026 sessions. Apply via the GitHub Secure Open Source Fund page.

Open call details

item.title: FLOSS/fund (Zerodha)
item.description:
Organisation: Zerodha (FLOSS/fund)

Location: Remote (worldwide)

Award: $10,000 to $100,000 per project (approximately $1,000,000 per year total budget). No application fee.

Duration: Project-based

Deadline: Rolling / undated

FLOSS/fund, backed by Zerodha, provides financial support to free and open-source software projects and maintainers. ELIGIBILITY: individuals and projects worldwide; applicants apply by publishing a funding.json manifest in their public repository as described on the fund's site. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with no deadline.

item.title: Sovereign Tech Fund
item.description:
Organisation: Sovereign Tech Agency (Germany)

Location: Remote (worldwide)

Award: Investment-style funding for open digital base technologies; amounts vary and are often EUR 100,000+. No application fee.

Duration: Project-based

Deadline: Rolling / undated

The Sovereign Tech Fund invests in the open digital infrastructure that underpins the modern internet, funding maintenance, security and development of critical open-source base technologies. ELIGIBILITY: individuals, companies and non-profits maintaining or developing critical open-source infrastructure; open worldwide. Applications are accepted on a rolling, year-round basis via the Sovereign Tech Fund page.

item.title: Wikimedia Conference Fund
item.description:
Organisation: Wikimedia Foundation

Location: Worldwide (subject to legal eligibility by country)

Award: From USD 10,000 per grant (no preset upper cap stated). No application fee.

Duration: Project-based. Processing approximately 3 months from submission to decision, plus 2-3 weeks for finalisation before disbursement.

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

Wikimedia Foundation grants supporting the organisation of local, regional and thematic conferences that bring Wikimedians together for knowledge sharing, skill development and professional networking. Two rounds per year. Round 1 deadline: 31 August 2026. Round 2 deadline: 1 February 2027. ELIGIBILITY: groups, organisations and Wikimedia affiliates; individuals may apply via a fiscal sponsor.

Open call details

item.title: Wikimedia Foundation Rapid Fund
item.description:
Organisation: Wikimedia Foundation

Location: Worldwide (subject to legal eligibility by country)

Award: $500 to $5,000 USD per grant (distributed in local-currency equivalent at time of application). Per-applicant cap $10,000/fiscal year; individuals may not hold multiple open Rapid Funds, organisations/groups limited to 2 open grants at a time.

Duration: 1 to 12 months per project

Deadline: Closed 01 Jul 2026

Quick-turnaround grants for individuals, Wikimedia community members, groups and affiliates running short-term, low-cost Wikimedia-focused projects: editathons, workshops, community meetups, education projects, cultural heritage initiatives, gender/diversity programmes, small-scale software development and content campaigns. Five cycles per year; upcoming deadlines: 1 July 2026, 1 September 2026, 1 November 2026, 1 February 2027, 1 April 2027. Approximately 2 months processing time per cycle. Standard track and Technical Projects track (Grants:Project/Rapid/Tech) share deadlines and amounts. Apply via the Wikimedia Foundation Grantee Portal (Fluxx) at https://wmf.fluxx.io/. Transfers run slower in June and December. CEE region applications routed via the CEE Hub from 1 April 2026. Ineligible: General Support Fund grantees, applicants on SDN lists, those with recent UCoC violations.

Open call details

item.title: OTF Internet Freedom Fund
item.description:
Organisation: Open Technology Fund (OTF)

Location: Worldwide

Award: $10,000 to $900,000 (sweet spot $50,000 to $200,000)

Duration: Up to 24 months (ideal: 6-12 months)

Deadline: Rolling / undated

Rolling-deadline fund for technology-focused projects that promote human rights, internet freedom and open societies. Funds anti-censorship, anti-surveillance, privacy-preserving and circumvention tools, plus applied research. Two-stage process: submit a Concept Note via the OTF online application system; reviewed monthly with feedback in 6-8 weeks. Open internationally.

Open call details

item.title: Internet Society Foundation: Research Grant Program 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Internet Society Foundation

Location: Worldwide

Award: $200,000 to $500,000 per project

Duration: Project-based

Deadline: Closed 22 May 2026

Research grants for innovative work deepening understanding of the Internet and its impact on society. Four focus areas: Inclusive Internet (structural barriers to digital participation), Greening the Internet (environmental impact and sustainability), Measuring Meaningful Connectivity (frameworks including AI, cloud, platform ecosystems), and A Trustworthy Internet (reliability, security, accountability). Open to individual researchers and organisations worldwide; underrepresented groups and Global Majority applicants strongly encouraged. Applications via Fluxx in English, French or Spanish.
